totalSugar.child: WHO Guideline (2015): 'We strongly recommend reducing free sugars intake to less than 10% of total energy intake, and suggest further reduction to below 5% (approx. 17g/day for pediatric needs) for additional health benefits. Exceeding this increases the risk of dental caries and unhealthy weight gain.'
totalSugar.teen: ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians (2024): 'Adolescents should limit free sugars to minimize the risk of metabolic syndrome. The upper limit for adolescent energy requirements is approximately 32g/day of added sugar.'
totalSugar.adult: WHO Guideline (2015): 'Adults should restrict free sugars to less than 10% of daily energy intake, optimally below 25g/day. High sugar intake is directly correlated with obesity and non-communicable diseases.'
totalSugar.elderly: ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians (2024): 'For the elderly, reducing sugar intake is critical to managing blood glucose levels and preventing metabolic complications. Intake should be strictly monitored.'
totalSugar.default: WHO Guideline (2015): 'Reducing free sugars to less than 10% of total energy intake reduces the risk of overweight, obesity, and tooth decay.'

addedSugar.child: WHO Guideline (2015): 'We strongly recommend reducing free sugars intake to less than 10% of total energy intake, and suggest further reduction to below 5% (approx. 17g/day for pediatric needs) for additional health benefits. Exceeding this increases the risk of dental caries and unhealthy weight gain.'
addedSugar.teen: ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians (2024): 'Adolescents should limit free sugars to minimize the risk of metabolic syndrome. The upper limit for adolescent energy requirements is approximately 32g/day of added sugar.'
addedSugar.adult: WHO Guideline (2015): 'Adults should restrict free sugars to less than 10% of daily energy intake, optimally below 25g/day. High sugar intake is directly correlated with obesity and non-communicable diseases.'
addedSugar.elderly: ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians (2024): 'For the elderly, reducing sugar intake is critical to managing blood glucose levels and preventing metabolic complications. Intake should be strictly monitored.'
addedSugar.default: WHO Guideline (2015): 'Reducing free sugars to less than 10% of total energy intake reduces the risk of overweight, obesity, and tooth decay.'

sodium.child: WHO Guideline (2012): 'Children should consume less than 2g of sodium per day, adjusted downward based on their energy requirements relative to adults, to prevent hypertension later in life.'
sodium.teen: WHO Guideline (2012): 'Adolescents should cap their sodium intake to less than 2g per day to maintain healthy blood pressure.'
sodium.adult: WHO Guideline (2012): 'Adults should consume less than 2g of sodium (equivalent to 5g of salt) per day to reduce blood pressure and the risk of cardiovascular disease, stroke, and coronary heart attack.'
sodium.elderly: ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians (2024): 'Elderly individuals are highly sensitive to sodium due to age-related renal changes and cardiovascular risk. Strict adherence to a low-sodium diet is advised.'
sodium.default: WHO Guideline (2012): 'High sodium consumption and insufficient potassium intake contribute to high blood pressure, which increases the risk of heart disease and stroke.'

saturatedFat.child: WHO Draft Guideline: 'Children should limit saturated fat intake to less than 10% of total energy intake to establish healthy cardiovascular baselines early in life.'
saturatedFat.teen: ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians (2024): 'Adolescents must balance fat intake, avoiding excess saturated fats which contribute to dyslipidemia.'
saturatedFat.adult: WHO Draft Guideline: 'Adults should limit saturated fat to less than 10% of total energy intake to lower the risk of non-communicable diseases.'
saturatedFat.elderly: ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians (2024): 'Saturated fat intake in the elderly must be restricted to manage cholesterol levels and reduce the incidence of atherosclerosis.'
saturatedFat.default: WHO Draft Guideline: 'Reducing saturated fat intake to less than 10% of total energy intake reduces the risk of cardiovascular disease.'

transFat.default: WHO REPLACE Action Package (2018): 'Industrially produced trans fats should be strictly eliminated from the food supply. Trans fat intake increases the risk of heart disease by 21% and deaths by 28%. There is no safe level of consumption.'

calories.default: ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians (2024): 'Caloric intake must be balanced with physical activity. Excessive energy-dense packaged foods displace nutrient-rich foods and drive the rising prevalence of overweight and obesity.'

cholesterol.default: ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians (2024): 'Dietary cholesterol should be monitored, particularly for individuals with elevated cardiovascular risk profiles.'

caffeine.child: FSSAI Regulations / Pediatric Consensus: 'Caffeine is not recommended for young children due to its effects on the developing neurological and cardiovascular systems.'
caffeine.teen: Pediatric Consensus: 'Adolescent caffeine intake should be severely limited to avoid sleep disruption, anxiety, and heart palpitations.'
caffeine.adult: General Health Guidance: 'Adults can safely consume up to 400mg of caffeine daily, but intake should be monitored to avoid side effects.'
caffeine.elderly: General Health Guidance: 'Elderly individuals should halve caffeine intake to account for slower metabolic clearance and sensitivity to cardiovascular stimulation.'
caffeine.default: General Health Guidance: 'Excessive caffeine can lead to jitteriness, insomnia, and increased heart rate.'
